newsitem.title: UK: United Utilities CEO Staples leaves co.
newsitem.headline: United Utilities CEO Staples leaves co.

text.p: Britain's United Utilities Plc said on Monday its chief executive, Brian Staples, left the company "following a loss of confidence in him by the board".
The company said it named Derek Green, currently managing director of the utility division, as its new chief executive.
"Both current trading, although slightly below the market's expectations, and the trading outlook are satisfactory," the company said, adding that its board was confident in its strategy.
United Utilities' shares dropped 40 pence to 729 by 1125 GMT.

The company said Derek Green would remain with the firm until 2000 following the conclusion of price reviews in the water and electricity sectors and Britain's transition to a competitive energy market.

Last month, United Utilities disappointed the market by reporting a lower-than-expected annual pretax profit of 444 million pounds ($745.4 million) before exceptionals compared to 389.2 million the previous year. ($ = 0.595 British Pounds)
